title: Keeping hope beyond a fallen picture
meaning: A shared idea can retain meaning after disappointment when hope allows its form and specific expectations to be reconsidered.
text: A shared aim can be sustained by belief in its significance. The Star in the physical position of Manipura describes actions that nourish the idea: gathering possibilities, offering support and leaving room for development. The Star in energy identifies the motive, giving form to an inspiring possibility. The Tower in emotions shows shock when the expected picture proves unsound. Hope, its practical support and the experience of collapse have different roles. Disappointment does not devalue your participation, but it does require acknowledging which part of the picture failed when it met circumstances.

Suppose you imagine a garden on a small balcony. You collect ideas and choose plants, but a trial arrangement shows there is insufficient space for the large design. **Hope can remain alive after its form is revised.** Losing a picture you already loved is unpleasant. Together you can choose what a smaller version preserves, without demanding immediate delight in the change or declaring the dream meaningless.

The difficulty is defending inspiration by denying the discovered limit. You add promises to restore the former feeling or reject the entire idea to avoid another disappointment. Either response leaves too little room for calmly considering facts. Support helps when it can bear the difference between hope and an available form. You can then choose a continuation whose meaning survives an imperfect first picture.
